module_title: Foundational Inventions and Discoveries in Physics
introduction: There are certain discoveries and inventions in physics that permanently altered human history and our daily lives. At this level, we cover the most fundamental and famous breakthroughs that are constantly tested in exams.

core_concepts.title: Laws of Motion and Universal Gravity
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Sir Isaac Newton (1687). 
Newton formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation in his famous book, 'Principia Mathematica'.

core_concepts.title: Electric Bulb (Incandescent Lamp)
core_concepts.description:
Inventor: Thomas Alva Edison (1879). 
He created the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb using a carbon filament.

core_concepts.title: X-Rays
core_concepts.description:
Discoverer: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen (1895). 
He discovered X-rays accidentally while experimenting with cathode rays. For this, he was awarded the 'First' ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

core_concepts.title: Telephone and Radio
core_concepts.description:
1. Telephone: Alexander Graham Bell (1876). 
2. Radio: Guglielmo Marconi (1901).

important_entities.name: Discovery vs. Invention
important_entities.significance: Exam tip: A 'Discovery' is finding something that already exists in nature (e.g., Gravity, X-rays). An 'Invention' is creating something entirely new that did not exist before (e.g., Bulb, Telephone).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Alfred Nobel invented 'Dynamite'. It was the massive fortune he made from this explosive invention that he later used to establish the prestigious 'Nobel Prizes'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate the word 'Marconi' with 'Macaroni'. You are eating Macaroni while listening to the Radio.

exam_strategy_tips: The most repeated question in SSC and Railway exams: 'Who discovered X-Rays?' Answer: W.K. Röntgen.
